summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential launch data, then build an agent product (Lighthouse, repo ask-soony) that rechecks the launch plan when new files drop, flags contradictions, and acts via supplier emails/calls with human approval. The final stretch was polishing role-based UI (Felix buyer vs Maren head of procurement) and preparing the 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Data analysis found the Collector's Edition misses launch despite an 'all ok' plan (overbooked art books, failed statues, new drops). A full product was built (poller, agents, Today/Launch/Routines/History pages, phone bridge, demo instance), PR #8 merged, and this segment added separate Felix/Maren sign-in and inboxes, History, a 'Fixed today' list, a rename to Lighthouse and role chips; commits are on main but not pushed, live not restarted, and the deck/video are not done.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks; the documented approach is polling the list and comparing SHA-256, since files are replaced under the same name.

Demo instance (:8001) deliberately runs without a portal token so data cannot change mid-demo; live (:8000) polls. A heartbeat must be gated on whether the instance polls (use the runner's own token check).
Live server serves the new web build immediately, but backend changes (sign-in choice, signoff inbox, who-decided field) only appear after restart.
Data in data/ is confidential and gitignored, but PR #8 merged 335 portal files into main under data/portal/; fix is git rm -r --cached data/portal (history keeps them).

Team workflow rules: ask before every push, no PRs unless asked, no attribution trailers, no em dashes, never print tokens, never approve/escalate cards on live data in tests (real supplier emails), experiment on state copies.
Fixed-today wins must come from confirmed-orders data (knows ETA and copies saved), not supplier reply fields, which wrongly listed Boise's 36,000 cards arriving after launch.
Entire checkpoints are only written when repo files change; hooks fire regardless (log says 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint').

code.finding: Only conflict between llm-task-update and main: both sides added new tests at the same spot; resolved by keeping both (360 tests pass).
New History page showing who decided what, how, and when, grouped by day; activity items gained a who-decided field and the cap rose from 40 to 200.

workflow: Subagent cross-checking 200 order confirmations and 59 scans against SAP surfaced the key discrepancies faster than manual reading.
Screenshot UI changes in a headless browser against a read-only preview server or a demo state copy, not live state.
When a UX suggestion would mostly repeat existing UI (green 'Covered' line), check what the page already shows before building; replaced it with the more valuable 'Fixed today'.
User corrections show to add information rather than replace it (role next to name, not instead of name).

friction: Entire hooks looked like they had not fired but only skipped the checkpoint because no files had changed.
Demo heartbeat showed 'Not checked since 08:30' because the demo never polls, which would look broken on stage.
Outbox sync overwrote concurrent actions (art book approval lost twice) until the append was moved under the lock.
Replies to side emails marked cards 'sent' and hid them; cp1252 German PO export crashed the paper check on a Sunday drop.
PR #8 opened with a merge conflict and brought portal data onto main, against challenge confidentiality rules.
Replacing names with roles and 'Ask Maren to approve' on Maren's own cases were unwanted changes needing rework.
Demo background loop does not auto-raise call alerts; realtime phone call cut off due to noise/concurrent responses (fixed).
open_items: Push main (about 10+ commits ahead of origin) and restart live server so sign-in choice, Maren's Waiting-for-your-OK and heartbeat appear.
Decide whether to remove data/portal from main (git rm -r --cached) and whether stored readings/golden.json stay in the repo.
Build the 6-slide pitch deck (using Lio figures, network map, Maren's 'We find out at the dock' quote) and record the video before the 12:00 hand-in.
Have not viewed the new sign-in and History pages in a real browser beyond headless screenshots.

Optional: delete duplicate routine 'Ask Hamburg to count book stock' on live; note to Hwaseong and message about Pulse emails; fix demo loop call alerts; top bar for Maren role; 'What still saves it' section on Launch.
After the demo, switch the OpenAI webhook back to https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev/hooks/openai.
Reconcile Collector's lid magnets false alarm, sleeve rev B vs C, and 78,000 unplanned pins with Soony (office-hours questions).
